newsitem.title: UK: Crude tanker rates stay low for Mideast/Japan.
newsitem.headline: Crude tanker rates stay low for Mideast/Japan.

text.p: Crude oil tanker rates for very large crude carriers (VLCCs) plying Mideast/U.S. routes consolidated their recent slide on Wednesday with news of another low fixture, shipbrokers said.
Chevron fixed the 279,000 tonne Grand Lady from the Mideast to the U.S. Gulf at W48.
"That is another poor fixture," one player said, adding that KPC's recent fixture of the 258,000 tonne Mariner at under W50 had set the tone for a lower trend.
Mideast/Japan routes were little changed, and the VLCC market was steady at W67.5.
European Suezmax markets were also suffering. Sun oil fixed the 135,000 tonne Romea Champion at W87.5, well below the W97.5 going rate for InterUK/Cont routes.
At least four tankers were moving southwards out of the North Sea because of poor rates, but rates remained weak in the Med too, ahead of the closure for maintenance of Novorossiisk's no. 1 terminal.
One broker said Libya's Zuetina terminal was closed becuase of bad weather but this could not be confirmed.
But the news was better in West Africa for owners of two- and one- million-barrel ships.
"West Africa is the place to be," one broker said.
A flurry of fixtures for 260,000 tonne ships to make westwards journeys were seen at around W62.5-W65.
A number of million-barrel ships were fixed to Europe at W97.5, and U.S. Gulf destinations were seen done at W90 and W100.

Fuel oil rates from the Baltic and the Black Sea were still holding up, with the 25,000 tonne Estere seen fixed by BP at W205 for a Lavera/Med route and similar sized vessels out of the Baltics seen at W195.
